# The only build instruction given to the AI

Read every document in `spec/` (PDFs can be converted with `pdftotext -layout`).
Then build CometFit exactly as our deliverables describe it, following `CLAUDE.md`.

Goal: a working implementation of every use case (UC-1 to UC-4) and every
functional requirement (FR-1 to FR-8) in the spec, with the architecture,
classes and sequence of interactions the spec's diagrams describe.

Environment facts (not product requirements): this machine has Java 23,
Maven 3.9, Docker 29, Node 22 and npm. The app must run locally on a laptop
and be demoable in a recorded video, so any mobile client must also run in a
browser. Finish in this order: backend + database, then client screens, then
tests, then a root `app/README.md` with step-by-step instructions to install
dependencies, configure environment variables and run the project locally.

When finished, make sure `TRACEABILITY.md` maps every FR and UC to the code
and tests that implement it, and `ASSUMPTIONS.md` lists every gap you filled.
# CometFit: implementation built only from Team 9's deliverables

SE 3354.006, Fall 2026, Team 9. This branch (`cleanroom-app`) holds the implemented CometFit app for the
+10 implementation bonus. The app was generated by an AI coding tool (Claude Code, model Claude Opus 5.5)
that was given **only our own project deliverables** plus the single prompt cited below.

- How to install and run the app: [`app/README.md`](app/README.md)
- How to verify the proof: [`proof/README.md`](proof/README.md)
- Requirement and use case to code map: [`TRACEABILITY.md`](TRACEABILITY.md)
- Gaps in our documents the AI had to fill: [`ASSUMPTIONS.md`](ASSUMPTIONS.md)

## Prompt citation

The AI received exactly one build instruction, committed before any code existed:

> Team 9 (Rafael Amador, Joseph Babuchna, Sean Chang, Aryansh Chaturvedi, Ameen Chougle, Richard Jang).
> "The only build instruction given to the AI." `PROMPT.md`, CometFit clean-room build, commit `7958f89`,
> 13 Nov 2026. Used with the rules file `CLAUDE.md` (same commit) and run with `proof/run-build.sh`.

Full text: [`PROMPT.md`](PROMPT.md). Rules: [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md). Any later update prompt is added
under `proof/prompts/` and cited here.

## Conditions (confirmed by the instructor)

On 13 Nov 2026 Dr. Barbara Maweu confirmed by email that the bonus conditions are: (1) the app may be
generated with an AI coding tool, (2) the AI may only be given our own deliverables (Proposal, Deliverable #1,
Deliverable #2 material), and (3) we show proof that only those were given to it; she added that the
README must include a citation of the prompt (above).

## Human input

The AI did the implementation. The team owns the project, so team members may correct the AI's assumptions
and clarify use cases. Every such decision is written down as its own input file in `spec/03-team-decisions/`,
hashed in `proof/MANIFEST.sha256` and committed before the AI acts on it, and listed in
`proof/HUMAN_INTERVENTIONS.md`. Nothing reaches the AI except files in `spec/`.

PDF export of Team 9's shared Google Doc "Team_09_SE3354_F26_Final_Project Report"
(the Deliverable 2 / final report), taken 2026-11-14 before submission.
Doc last modified 2026-11-14T01:28:30Z. Sections 2-5 are written by the team;
Section 6 (Conclusion) is not written yet.
# Team decisions

Corrections and clarifications made by Team 9 members after reviewing the AI's assumptions or output.
Each file: `TD-n.md` with date, team member, which assumption (A-n) or use case it changes, and the decision.
These are part of our deliverables and are fed to the AI like any other spec file.
# TD-1: Easier two-factor setup and sign-in

- **Date:** 2026-11-13
- **Decided by:** Team 9 (approved by Rafael Amador, project manager, after testing the stage-1 app)
- **Changes:** Assumptions A-3 and A-6 (account setup and login flow). Still meets NFR Security (username + password + TOTP).

## Decision
1. After sign-up, show an **"Add to authenticator app"** button that opens the phone's authenticator app with the CometFit account already filled in, and a **"Copy setup key"** button as a backup.
2. Show a **QR code** of the setup key only when the app runs on a larger screen (for example a laptop browser), where a phone can scan it.
3. At sign-in, offer **"Remember this device for 30 days."** On a remembered device the student signs in with username and password only; the 6-digit code is required again on a new device or after 30 days.

## Why
Testing showed that typing a raw secret into an authenticator and entering a code on every sign-in is too slow for a student app, and a QR code on the phone's own screen cannot be scanned by that phone.
# TD-2: Demo accounts share their data

- **Date:** 2026-11-13
- **Decided by:** Team 9 (approved by Rafael Amador, project manager, after testing the stage-1 app)
- **Changes:** Assumption A-18 (default sharing) for the seeded demo accounts only.

## Decision
The seeded demo students (alice and bob) start with all data sharing turned on (calories, water, steps, UREC visits) and have some activity history, so UC-3 (friends' progress and leaderboard) shows real numbers in the recorded demo.
Real new accounts keep the current behavior: nothing is shared until the student turns it on (NFR Ethical / Legislative-Privacy).

## Why
In testing, the friends screen showed "Not shared" for every stat and the leaderboard listed only one person, so UC-3 could not be demonstrated.
# TD-3: Water refill map is out of scope

- **Date:** 2026-11-13
- **Decided by:** Team 9 (approved by Rafael Amador, project manager)
- **Changes:** Clarifies a conflict between the Proposal and Deliverable #1.

## Decision
The Proposal (Section 3, Project Objectives) mentions "a map showing the different and closest areas to refill their water." This feature was not carried into the Deliverable #1 functional requirements (FR-1 to FR-8) or use cases (UC-1 to UC-4). The team confirms it is **out of scope** for this version: do not build it. Record it in ASSUMPTIONS.md as an intentionally excluded Proposal feature.

## Why
The team narrowed scope to the core tracking features when requirements were finalized. This change is explained in the report's Conclusion (Section 6).
# CometFit

- Team Number: 9
- Team Name: Team 9

`src/` currently contains the source code for checking the logging water intake functionality.

The tech stack is as follows:
- Java for logging functionality
- MySQL for database operations
- Docker for containerized instances
- JUnit for unit testing

To run the program, navigate to `src/` and run `run.sh`. This will automatically bring the docker container up, compile and run the java tests, and tear down the docker container.# Team repo code

Unit code and tests written by Team 9 (Richard Jang) for Deliverable 2, Section 4.2/4.3.

    userId VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL REFERENCES USERS(user_id),
    amount FLOAT NOT NULL,
    loggedAt TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

# Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1") is silent or
ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app"
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security
A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)
A-8 | Where the water-bottle size lives (Prop: "volume of the user's water bottle … number of refills"; SD-1 "log water (bottle size / refill)"; class diagram has no field) | Added `bottleSizeMl` to Student (set in Profile → Goals). The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). # CometFit local stack: PostgreSQL = the "Encrypted Database" of Deliverable 1 §5.3.2 (A-2).
# Start:  docker compose up -d db        (from the app/ folder)
# The server can also run in the container: docker compose up -d --build
services:
  db:
    image: postgres:16-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_DB: cometfit
      POSTGRES_USER: cometfit
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
    ports:
      - "5432:5432"
    volumes:
      - cometfit-db:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "pg_isready -U cometfit -d cometfit"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 10

  server:
    build: ./server
    profiles: ["full"]
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      DB_URL: jdbc:postgresql://db:5432/cometfit
      DB_USER: cometfit
      DB_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
      COMETFIT_DATA_KEY: ${COMETFIT_DATA_KEY:-Q29tZXRGaXQtZGV2LW9ubHkta2V5LWNoYW5nZS1tZSE=}
      COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY: ${COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY:-dev-integration-key}
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"

volumes:
  cometfit-db:

# CometFit server configuration.
# Default profile = PostgreSQL (the "Encrypted Database" of Deliverable 1 §5.3.2), run via docker-compose.
# Profile "h2" = embedded file database for laptops without Docker (ASSUMPTIONS A-2).
server:
  port: ${PORT:8080}

spring:
  application:
    name: cometfit-server
  datasource:
    url: ${DB_URL:jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/cometfit}
    username: ${DB_USER:cometfit}
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD:cometfit}
  jpa:
    open-in-view: false
    hibernate:
      ddl-auto: validate
    properties:
      hibernate.jdbc.time_zone: UTC
  flyway:
    enabled: true
  servlet:
    multipart:
      max-file-size: 10MB
      max-request-size: 10MB

management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health

cometfit:
  # Local day boundary for daily summaries (A-9)
  zone: ${COMETFIT_ZONE:America/Chicago}
  # Session lifetime in hours (A-6)
  session-hours: ${COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS:12}
  # Base64 AES-256 key used to encrypt sensitive user fields at rest (NFR Security, A-5).
  # The default is a DEVELOPMENT key only. Set COMETFIT_DATA_KEY in any shared environment.
  data-key: ${COMETFIT_DATA_KEY:Q29tZXRGaXQtZGV2LW9ubHkta2V5LWNoYW5nZS1tZSE=}
  # Shared secret that external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) present (A-12).
  integration-key: ${COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY:dev-integration-key}
  # Monitoring service stub interval (SD-4 "loop every interval", MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec)
  monitoring:
    check-interval-sec: ${COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC:30}
    stub-enabled: ${COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB:true}
  # Seed demo accounts (developer + two students) with fixed TOTP secrets (A-14). Demo only.
  seed-demo: ${COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO:true}
  # Allowed browser origins for the web build of the mobile client
  cors-origins: ${COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS:http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006}

---
spring:
  config:
    activate:
      on-profile: h2
  datasource:
    url: ${DB_URL:jdbc:h2:file:./data/cometfit;MODE=PostgreSQL;DATABASE_TO_LOWER=TRUE;DEFAULT_NULL_ORDERING=HIGH}
    username: ${DB_USER:sa}
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD:}

1	# CometFit — local setup and demo guide
2	
3	CometFit (SE 3354 Team 9) is a student health-tracking app: meals and water (UC-1), activity and UREC visits (UC-2),
4	friends' progress (UC-3), and developer monitoring and control (UC-4). It was built only from the team's Proposal and
5	Deliverable 1. `../TRACEABILITY.md` maps every requirement to code and tests. `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` lists every gap
6	that had to be filled.
7	
8	```
9	app/
10	├── server/            Spring Boot REST server: API gateway, auth gateway, Nutrition / Activity / Social / Admin services
11	├── client/            Expo (React Native) mobile app — also runs in a web browser for the demo
12	├── tools/             totp.mjs (prints sign-in codes), smoke.mjs (end-to-end HTTP check)
13	└── docker-compose.yml PostgreSQL database (and optionally the server)
14	```
15	
16	The architecture follows Deliverable 1 §5.3 (client-server): the mobile client talks to one REST API, and every call
17	goes through the auth gateway (password + TOTP sessions, permissions list) and the module (feature-flag) check before
18	it reaches a service. Outside systems (AI food recognition, UTD Dining menus, smart devices, the UREC card reader,
19	the monitoring service and the alert channel) are **stubs**. They are labelled `*** STUB ***` in the code and listed at
20	the end of this file.
21	
22	---
23	
24	## 1. Install prerequisites
25	
26	| Tool | Version used | Check with |
27	|---|---|---|
28	| Java JDK | 21 or newer (built with 23) | `java -version` |
29	| Maven | 3.9+ | `mvn -v` |
30	| Node.js + npm | Node 22+ | `node -v` |
31	| Docker Desktop | optional, for PostgreSQL | `docker version` |
32	
33	Without Docker, use the embedded H2 database (step 3, option B).
34	
35	## 2. Install dependencies
36	
37	```bash
38	# server (downloads the Maven dependencies)
39	cd app/server
40	mvn -DskipTests package
41	
42	# client
43	cd ../client
44	npm install
45	```
46	
47	## 3. Configure environment variables
48	
49	Every variable has a development default, so **nothing needs to be set for a local demo**. For anything shared, set
50	at least `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`.
51	
52	### Server (`app/server`)
53	
54	| Variable | Default | Purpose |
55	|---|---|---|
56	| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
57	| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/cometfit` (H2 file `./data/cometfit` with the `h2` profile) | JDBC URL |
58	| `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` | `cometfit` / `cometfit` | Database login |
59	| `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` | development key | Base64 32-byte AES key that encrypts emails and TOTP secrets at rest. Generate one: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`. **Changing it makes existing accounts unreadable.** |
60	| `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY` | `dev-integration-key` | Shared secret that the UREC card reader and the external monitor send in the `X-Integration-Key` header |
61	| `COMETFIT_ZONE` | `America/Chicago` | Time zone that defines "today" for daily totals |
62	| `COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS` | `12` | Session lifetime |
63	| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC` | `30` | Health-check interval of the monitoring stub |
64	| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB` | `true` | Run the built-in monitoring-service stub |
65	| `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO` | `true` | Create the demo accounts below on start-up |
66	| `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006` | Browser origins allowed to call the API |
67	
68	### Client (`app/client`)
69	
70	| Variable | Default | Purpose |
71	|---|---|---|
72	| `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` (`http://10.0.2.2:8080` on the Android emulator) | Server base URL |
73	
74	To set variables: in bash, `export NAME=value`. In PowerShell, `$env:NAME = "value"`. You can also put client
75	variables in `app/client/.env` (this file is git-ignored).
76	
77	## 4. Run the project locally
78	
79	### Start the database and server
80	
81	**Option A — PostgreSQL in Docker (default profile)**
82	
83	```bash
84	cd app
85	docker compose up -d db          # PostgreSQL 16 on localhost:5432
86	cd server
87	mvn spring-boot:run
88	```
89	
90	**Option B — no Docker (embedded H2 file database)**
91	
92	```bash
93	cd app/server
94	mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=h2
95	```
96	
97	Either way, Flyway creates the schema on first start. The server is ready when
98	<http://localhost:8080/actuator/health> shows `{"status":"UP"}`. The H2 data is stored in `app/server/data/`;
99	delete that folder to start over.
100	
101	*(Optional: run everything in containers with `docker compose --profile full up -d --build`.)*
102	
103	### Start the client
104	
105	```bash
106	cd app/client
107	npm run web            # opens http://localhost:8081 in the browser
108	```
109	
110	For a phone-like view in the browser, use the dev tools' device toolbar. On a real phone, run `npx expo start` and
111	open the app in Expo Go. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to your laptop's LAN address, for example
112	`http://192.168.1.20:8080`.
113	
114	### Sign in
115	
116	| Username | Password | TOTP secret | Role |
117	|---|---|---|---|
118	| `alice` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITALICE234` | Student |
119	| `bob` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITBOBBY567` | Student |
120	| `dev` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITDEVADMIN` | Developer (admin dashboard) |
121	
122	Every sign-in needs the current 6-digit code. Get it from any authenticator app (add the secret), or from:
123	
124	```bash
125	node app/tools/totp.mjs COMETFITALICE234
126	```
127	
128	New students can register from the sign-in screen. The app then shows their own TOTP secret once.
129	
130	## 5. Run the tests
131	
132	```bash
133	cd app/server && mvn test        # 38 API/unit tests on H2, one test class per use case (Uc1..Uc4) + security
134	cd app/client && npm test        # client unit tests (Node test runner)
135	cd app/client && npm run typecheck
136	
137	# End-to-end over real HTTP against a running server (uses the demo accounts):
138	node app/tools/smoke.mjs http://localhost:8080
139	```
140	
141	## 6. Demo script (about 5 minutes)
142	
143	1. **UC-1** — Sign in as `alice`. On **Log**, tap *+1 refill*, then log a meal manually. Switch to *Dining menu* →
144	   *Dining Hall* → *Add* an item. Switch to *Photo (AI)* and pick any image, edit the estimate, then *Confirm & save*.
145	   **Today** shows calories, macros, water progress and the low-water message.
146	2. **Safety** — in **Profile → Daily goals**, enter 800 kcal or 6000 ml and watch the warnings appear.
147	3. **UC-2** — **Activity** → *Connect smart device* → *Allow* (simulated health prompt) → *Sync now*. Then
148	   *Simulate UREC card swipe*, which earns +10 points and appears in the visit history.
149	4. **UC-3** — **Friends** → search `bob` → *Profile* → *Add friend*. In a second browser window (or a private
150	   window), sign in as `bob` and *Accept*. As `alice`, turn sharing on under *What my friends can see*. As `bob`,
151	   open alice's *Stats* and the leaderboard.
152	5. **UC-4** — Sign in as `dev`. The dashboard shows uptime % and per-service status. Click *Simulate outage* on a
153	   service to see a downtime alert and an incident, then end it. *Disable* "Friends & Leaderboard" and switch to
154	   bob's window: the Friends tab shows the maintenance notice while the other tabs keep working. *Re-enable* it.
155	
156	## 7. Stubs (external systems from the spec)
157	
158	| External actor in the spec | Interface | Stub implementation |
159	|---|---|---|
160	| AI Food Recognition Service (UC-1) | `services/AIFoodService` | `stubs/FakeAIFoodService` — deterministic estimate from the image hash |
161	| UTD Dining menu data (UC-1, FR-8) | `services/UtdDiningFeed` | `stubs/StubUtdDiningFeed` — fixed sample menu for "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" |
162	| Smart Device pairing (UC-2) | `services/SmartDeviceGateway` | `stubs/FakeSmartDeviceGateway` — always pairs, except device ids starting with `FAIL` |
163	| Smart Device readings + health permission (UC-2) | client `src/smartDevice.ts` `SmartDeviceAdapter` | `FakeSmartDevice` — simulated steps / heart rate |
164	| UREC Card Reader (UC-2) | `POST /api/activity/visits` with the integration key | `stubs/FakeUrecCardReader` — the "Simulate UREC card swipe" button |
165	| Monitoring Service (UC-4) | `POST /api/admin/health-check` with the integration key | `stubs/MonitoringAgentStub` — timer inside the server |
166	| Downtime alert channel (UC-4) | `services/AlertNotifier` | `stubs/LoggingAlertNotifier` — logs the alert and shows it on the dashboard |
167	| A real outage (demo only) | — | `stubs/OutageSimulator` — the "Simulate outage" button |
168	
169	## 8. REST API overview
170	
171	All endpoints except register, login and health need `Authorization: Bearer <token>`.
172	
173	| Area | Endpoints |
174	|---|---|
175	| Auth | `POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` |
176	| Profile (FR-3) | `GET/PUT /api/profile`, `PUT /api/profile/password`, `PUT /api/profile/goals` |
177	| Nutrition (UC-1) | `POST /api/nutrition/meals/photo`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu/locations`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu?location=`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/meals`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/water`, `GET /api/nutrition/summary` |
178	| Activity (UC-2) | `POST/GET /api/activity/devices`, `DELETE /api/activity/devices/{id}`, `POST /api/activity/steps`, `GET /api/activity/records`, `POST /api/activity/visits` (reader), `GET /api/activity/visits`, `POST /api/activity/stub-reader/swipe` |
179	| Social (UC-3) | `GET /api/social/users/search?q=`, `GET /api/social/users/{id}`, `POST/GET /api/social/requests`, `POST /api/social/requests/{id}/accept\|decline`, `GET /api/social/friends`, `DELETE /api/social/friends/{id}`, `GET/PUT /api/social/consent`, `GET /api/social/friends/{id}/stats`, `GET /api/social/leaderboard` |
180	| Modules (FR-5) | `GET /api/modules`, `GET /api/modules/{id}` |
181	| Admin (UC-4) | `GET /api/admin/access`, `GET /api/admin/uptime?hours=`, `POST /api/admin/uptime/check-now`, `GET /api/admin/alerts`, `GET /api/admin/modules`, `POST /api/admin/modules/{id}/disable\|enable`, `POST /api/admin/health-check` (monitor), `POST /api/admin/stub/outage` |
182	
183	When a module is disabled, its endpoints answer `503 {"code":"MODULE_DISABLED"}` and the app shows a maintenance
184	notice.
185	
186	## Troubleshooting
187	
188	- **"Cannot reach the CometFit server"** in the app: the server isn't running, or `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` is wrong.
189	- **Login fails with a correct password:** the 6-digit code is wrong or expired, or the laptop clock is off.
190	- **Port 8080 already in use:** set `PORT=8090` before starting the server, and set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8090` for the client.
191	- **CORS error in the browser:** add the page's origin to `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS`.
192	- **"Could not decrypt field":** `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` changed after the accounts were created. Restore the old key or reset the database.
193

friends' progress (UC-3), and developer monitoring and control (UC-4). It was built only from the team's Proposal and
Deliverable 1. `../TRACEABILITY.md` maps every requirement to code and tests. `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` lists every gap
that had to be filled.

```
app/
├── server/            Spring Boot REST server: API gateway, auth gateway, Nutrition / Activity / Social / Admin services
├── client/            Expo (React Native) mobile app — also runs in a web browser for the demo
├── tools/             totp.mjs (prints sign-in codes), smoke.mjs (end-to-end HTTP check)
└── docker-compose.yml PostgreSQL database (and optionally the server)
```

goes through the auth gateway (password + TOTP sessions, permissions list) and the module (feature-flag) check before
it reaches a service. Outside systems (AI food recognition, UTD Dining menus, smart devices, the UREC card reader,
the monitoring service and the alert channel) are **stubs**. They are labelled `*** STUB ***` in the code and listed at
the end of this file.

---

| Tool | Version used | Check with |
|---|---|---|
| Java JDK | 21 or newer (built with 23) | `java -version` |
| Maven | 3.9+ | `mvn -v` |
| Node.js + npm | Node 22+ | `node -v` |
| Docker Desktop | optional, for PostgreSQL | `docker version` |

Without Docker, use the embedded H2 database (step 3, option B).

## 2. Install dependencies

```bash
# server (downloads the Maven dependencies)
cd app/server
mvn -DskipTests package

# client
cd ../client
npm install
```

## 3. Configure environment variables

Every variable has a development default, so **nothing needs to be set for a local demo**. For anything shared, set
at least `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD` and `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`.

### Server (`app/server`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/cometfit` (H2 file `./data/cometfit` with the `h2` profile) | JDBC URL |
| `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` | `cometfit` / `cometfit` | Database login |
| `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` | development key | Base64 32-byte AES key that encrypts emails and TOTP secrets at rest. Generate one: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`. **Changing it makes existing accounts unreadable.** |
| `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY` | `dev-integration-key` | Shared secret that the UREC card reader and the external monitor send in the `X-Integration-Key` header |
| `COMETFIT_ZONE` | `America/Chicago` | Time zone that defines "today" for daily totals |
| `COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS` | `12` | Session lifetime |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC` | `30` | Health-check interval of the monitoring stub |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB` | `true` | Run the built-in monitoring-service stub |
| `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO` | `true` | Create the demo accounts below on start-up |
| `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006` | Browser origins allowed to call the API |

### Client (`app/client`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` (`http://10.0.2.2:8080` on the Android emulator) | Server base URL |

To set variables: in bash, `export NAME=value`. In PowerShell, `$env:NAME = "value"`. You can also put client
variables in `app/client/.env` (this file is git-ignored).

## 4. Run the project locally

### Start the database and server

**Option A — PostgreSQL in Docker (default profile)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up -d db          # PostgreSQL 16 on localhost:5432
cd server
mvn spring-boot:run
```

**Option B — no Docker (embedded H2 file database)**

```bash
cd app/server
mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=h2

<http://localhost:8080/actuator/health> shows `{"status":"UP"}`. The H2 data is stored in `app/server/data/`;
delete that folder to start over.

*(Optional: run everything in containers with `docker compose --profile full up -d --build`.)*

### Start the client

```bash
cd app/client
npm run web            # opens http://localhost:8081 in the browser
```

open the app in Expo Go. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to your laptop's LAN address, for example
`http://192.168.1.20:8080`.

### Sign in

| Username | Password | TOTP secret | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alice` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITALICE234` | Student |
| `bob` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITBOBBY567` | Student |
| `dev` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITDEVADMIN` | Developer (admin dashboard) |

```bash

## 5. Run the tests

```bash

cd app/client && npm test        # client unit tests (Node test runner)
cd app/client && npm run typecheck

# End-to-end over real HTTP against a running server (uses the demo accounts):
node app/tools/smoke.mjs http://localhost:8080
```

## 6. Demo script (about 5 minutes)

1. **UC-1** — Sign in as `alice`. On **Log**, tap *+1 refill*, then log a meal manually. Switch to *Dining menu* →
   *Dining Hall* → *Add* an item. Switch to *Photo (AI)* and pick any image, edit the estimate, then *Confirm & save*.

3. **UC-2** — **Activity** → *Connect smart device* → *Allow* (simulated health prompt) → *Sync now*. Then

## 8. REST API overview

| Area | Endpoints |
|---|---|
| Auth | `POST /api/auth/register`, `POST /api/auth/login`, `POST /api/auth/logout`, `GET /api/auth/me` |
| Profile (FR-3) | `GET/PUT /api/profile`, `PUT /api/profile/password`, `PUT /api/profile/goals` |
| Nutrition (UC-1) | `POST /api/nutrition/meals/photo`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu/locations`, `GET /api/nutrition/menu?location=`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/meals`, `POST/GET /api/nutrition/water`, `GET /api/nutrition/summary` |
| Activity (UC-2) | `POST/GET /api/activity/devices`, `DELETE /api/activity/devices/{id}`, `POST /api/activity/steps`, `GET /api/activity/records`, `POST /api/activity/visits` (reader), `GET /api/activity/visits`, `POST /api/activity/stub-reader/swipe` |
| Social (UC-3) | `GET /api/social/users/search?q=`, `GET /api/social/users/{id}`, `POST/GET /api/social/requests`, `POST /api/social/requests/{id}/accept\|decline`, `GET /api/social/friends`, `DELETE /api/social/friends/{id}`, `GET/PUT /api/social/consent`, `GET /api/social/friends/{id}/stats`, `GET /api/social/leaderboard` |
| Modules (FR-5) | `GET /api/modules`, `GET /api/modules/{id}` |
| Admin (UC-4) | `GET /api/admin/access`, `GET /api/admin/uptime?hours=`, `POST /api/admin/uptime/check-now`, `GET /api/admin/alerts`, `GET /api/admin/modules`, `POST /api/admin/modules/{id}/disable\|enable`, `POST /api/admin/health-check` (monitor), `POST /api/admin/stub/outage` |

When a module is disabled, its endpoints answer `503 {"code":"MODULE_DISABLED"}` and the app shows a maintenance
notice.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Cannot reach the CometFit server"** in the app: the server isn't running, or `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` is wrong.
- **Login fails with a correct password:** the 6-digit code is wrong or expired, or the laptop clock is off.
- **Port 8080 already in use:** set `PORT=8090` before starting the server, and set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL=http://localhost:8090` for the client.
- **CORS error in the browser:** add the page's origin to `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS`.
- **"Could not decrypt field":** `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` changed after the accounts were created. Restore the old key or reset the database.

content.text: Now the MySQL switch (D-1). Rewriting the baseline migration in MySQL syntax (fresh database, so no migration history is lost) with table-level foreign keys, since MySQL ignores inline `REFERENCES`.

input.content:
-- CometFit schema. Every table maps to a class of the Deliverable 1 / Deliverable 2 draft class diagram
-- (D1 §5.2 = D2 §2.5.2, identical).
-- Database product: MySQL 8.4 (team repo code README "MySQL for database operations", db/docker-compose.yml
-- `mysql:8.4`; supersedes A-2). Also runs on H2 in MySQL mode for the automated tests.
-- Foreign keys are table constraints because MySQL ignores inline column REFERENCES.
-- Timestamps are DATETIME(6), stored in UTC (hibernate.jdbc.time_zone=UTC).

-- Users and Security package: User (abstract) <- Student, Developer
CREATE TABLE users (
    id              BIGINT       NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_type       VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL,           -- STUDENT | DEVELOPER
    username        VARCHAR(40)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    password_hash   VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    email_enc       VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,           -- AES-GCM encrypted (NFR Security)
    totp_secret_enc VARCHAR(512) NOT NULL,           -- AES-GCM encrypted (NFR Security)
    display_name    VARCHAR(80)  NOT NULL,
    is_public       BOOLEAN      NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    -- Student
    calorie_goal    INTEGER,
    water_goal_ml   INTEGER,
    step_goal       INTEGER,
    bottle_size_ml  INTEGER,                         -- A-8
    -- Developer
    admin_role      VARCHAR(40),
    created_at      DATETIME(6)  NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE developer_permissions (
    user_id    BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    permission VARCHAR(60) NOT NULL,
    PRIMARY KEY (user_id, permission),
    CONSTRAINT fk_devperm_user FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE sessions (
    token      VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    user_id    BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    created_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    expires_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_session_user FOREIGN KEY (user_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

-- Domain Data package
CREATE TABLE water_entries (
    id         BIGINT      NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    volume_ml  INTEGER     NOT NULL,
    logged_at  DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_water_student FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);
CREATE INDEX ix_water_student_time ON water_entries(student_id, logged_at);

CREATE TABLE dining_items (
    id          BIGINT       NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    external_id VARCHAR(60)  NOT NULL UNIQUE,        -- id in the UTD Dining feed
    name        VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    location    VARCHAR(80)  NOT NULL,
    calories    INTEGER      NOT NULL,
    protein_g   DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    carbs_g     DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    fat_g       DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE meal_entries (
    id             BIGINT       NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id     BIGINT       NOT NULL,
    food_name      VARCHAR(120) NOT NULL,
    calories       INTEGER      NOT NULL,
    protein_g      DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    carbs_g        DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    fat_g          DOUBLE PRECISION NOT NULL,
    source         VARCHAR(16)  NOT NULL,            -- MealSource: MANUAL | PHOTO | DINING_MENU
    dining_item_id BIGINT,
    logged_at      DATETIME(6)  NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_meal_student FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_meal_dining FOREIGN KEY (dining_item_id) REFERENCES dining_items(id)
);
CREATE INDEX ix_meal_student_time ON meal_entries(student_id, logged_at);

CREATE TABLE smart_devices (
    id          BIGINT      NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    device_id   VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL UNIQUE,
    device_type VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    platform    VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE device_links (
    id              BIGINT      NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id      BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    smart_device_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    linked_at       DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    status          VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,             -- LINKED | UNLINKED
    CONSTRAINT fk_link_student FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_link_device FOREIGN KEY (smart_device_id) REFERENCES smart_devices(id)
);

CREATE TABLE activity_records (
    id              BIGINT      NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id      BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    smart_device_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    steps           INTEGER     NOT NULL,
    heart_rate      INTEGER,
    recorded_at     DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_activity_student FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_activity_device FOREIGN KEY (smart_device_id) REFERENCES smart_devices(id)
);
CREATE INDEX ix_activity_student_time ON activity_records(student_id, recorded_at);

CREATE TABLE urec_card_readers (
    reader_id VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    location  VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL
);

CREATE TABLE rec_visits (
    id         BIGINT      NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    reader_id  VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    visited_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_visit_student FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_visit_reader FOREIGN KEY (reader_id) REFERENCES urec_card_readers(reader_id)
);
CREATE INDEX ix_visit_student_time ON rec_visits(student_id, visited_at);

CREATE TABLE friend_requests (
    id          BIGINT      NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    sender_id   BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    receiver_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    status      VARCHAR(16) NOT NULL,                -- PENDING | ACCEPTED | DECLINED
    sent_at     DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_freq_sender FOREIGN KEY (sender_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_freq_receiver FOREIGN KEY (receiver_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE friendships (
    id        BIGINT      NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    user_a_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    user_b_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    since     DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT uq_friendship UNIQUE (user_a_id, user_b_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_friend_a FOREIGN KEY (user_a_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_friend_b FOREIGN KEY (user_b_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE consent_settings (
    student_id     BIGINT  NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    share_calories BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    share_water    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    share_steps    BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    share_visits   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    CONSTRAINT fk_consent_student FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE point_accounts (
    student_id BIGINT  NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    balance    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    CONSTRAINT fk_points_student FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE point_transactions (
    id         BIGINT      NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    student_id BIGINT      NOT NULL,
    amount     INTEGER     NOT NULL,
    reason     VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    created_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    CONSTRAINT fk_ptx_account FOREIGN KEY (student_id) REFERENCES point_accounts(student_id) ON DELETE CASCADE
);

CREATE TABLE app_modules (
    module_id VARCHAR(32) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY,
    name      VARCHAR(80) NOT NULL,
    enabled   BOOLEAN     NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE
);

CREATE TABLE uptime_records (
    id           BIGINT      NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT PRIMARY KEY,
    checked_at   DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    service_name VARCHAR(40) NOT NULL,
    is_up        BOOLEAN     NOT NULL,
    response_ms  INTEGER     NOT NULL
);
CREATE INDEX ix_uptime_time ON uptime_records(checked_at);

-- Seed: app modules a developer can disable (FR-5, A-11)
INSERT INTO app_modules (module_id, name, enabled) VALUES ('NUTRITION', 'Nutrition & Hydration', TRUE);
INSERT INTO app_modules (module_id, name, enabled) VALUES ('ACTIVITY', 'Activity & UREC Visits', TRUE);
INSERT INTO app_modules (module_id, name, enabled) VALUES ('SOCIAL', 'Friends & Leaderboard', TRUE);

-- Seed: one registered UREC card reader (UC-2, A-12)
INSERT INTO urec_card_readers (reader_id, location) VALUES ('UREC-FRONT-1', 'UREC front desk');

# CometFit server configuration.
# Default profile = PostgreSQL (the "Encrypted Database" of Deliverable 1 §5.3.2), run via docker-compose.
# Profile "h2" = embedded file database for laptops without Docker (ASSUMPTIONS A-2).
server:
  port: ${PORT:8080}

spring:
  application:
    name: cometfit-server
  datasource:
    url: ${DB_URL:jdbc:postgresql://localhost:5432/cometfit}
    username: ${DB_USER:cometfit}
    password: ${DB_PASSWORD:cometfit}
  jpa:
    open-in-view: false
    hibernate:
      ddl-auto: validate
    properties:
      hibernate.jdbc.time_zone: UTC
  flyway:
    enabled: true
  servlet:
    multipart:
      max-file-size: 10MB
      max-request-size: 10MB

management:
  endpoints:
    web:
      exposure:
        include: health

cometfit:
  # Local day boundary for daily summaries (A-9)
  zone: ${COMETFIT_ZONE:America/Chicago}
  # Session lifetime in hours (A-6)
  session-hours: ${COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS:12}
  # Base64 AES-256 key used to encrypt sensitive user fields at rest (NFR Security, A-5).
  # The default is a DEVELOPMENT key only. Set COMETFIT_DATA_KEY in any shared environment.
  data-key: ${COMETFIT_DATA_KEY:Q29tZXRGaXQtZGV2LW9ubHkta2V5LWNoYW5nZS1tZSE=}
  # Shared secret that external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) present (A-12).
  integration-key: ${COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY:dev-integration-key}
  # Monitoring service stub interval (SD-4 "loop every interval", MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec)
  monitoring:
    check-interval-sec: ${COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC:30}
    stub-enabled: ${COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB:true}
  # Seed demo accounts (developer + two students) with fixed TOTP secrets (A-14). Demo only.
  seed-demo: ${COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO:true}
  # Allowed browser origins for the web build of the mobile client
  cors-origins: ${COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS:http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006}

input.content:
# CometFit local stack. Start everything from the app/ folder with:   docker compose up --build
#   db     = MySQL 8.4, the "Encrypted Database" of D1 §5.3.2. Product and image from the team repo code
#            (spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md "MySQL for database operations", db/docker-compose.yml `mysql:8.4`).
#   server = CometFit REST server (API gateway, auth gateway, services; D1 §5.3.2).
# Fresh demo data: docker compose down -v   (deletes the database volume), then up again.
services:
  db:
    image: mysql:8.4
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: cometfit
      MYSQL_USER: cometfit
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-root}
    ports:
      - "3306:3306"
    volumes:
      - cometfit-mysql:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "localhost", "-u", "cometfit", "-p${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  server:
    build: ./server
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      DB_URL: jdbc:mysql://db:3306/cometfit
      DB_USER: cometfit
      DB_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
      COMETFIT_DATA_KEY: ${COMETFIT_DATA_KEY:-Q29tZXRGaXQtZGV2LW9ubHkta2V5LWNoYW5nZS1tZSE=}
      COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY: ${COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY:-dev-integration-key}
      COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO: ${COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO:-true}
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/actuator/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

volumes:
  cometfit-mysql:

# CometFit local stack. Start everything from the app/ folder with:   docker compose up --build
#   db     = MySQL 8.4, the "Encrypted Database" of D1 §5.3.2. Product and image from the team repo code
#            (spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md "MySQL for database operations", db/docker-compose.yml `mysql:8.4`).
#   server = CometFit REST server (API gateway, auth gateway, services; D1 §5.3.2).
# Fresh demo data: docker compose down -v   (deletes the database volume), then up again.
services:
  db:
    image: mysql:8.4
    environment:
      MYSQL_DATABASE: cometfit
      MYSQL_USER: cometfit
      MYSQL_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
      MYSQL_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${DB_ROOT_PASSWORD:-root}
    ports:
      - "3306:3306"
    volumes:
      - cometfit-mysql:/var/lib/mysql
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "mysqladmin", "ping", "-h", "localhost", "-u", "cometfit", "-p${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}"]
      interval: 3s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

  server:
    build: ./server
    depends_on:
      db:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      DB_URL: jdbc:mysql://db:3306/cometfit
      DB_USER: cometfit
      DB_PASSWORD: ${DB_PASSWORD:-cometfit}
      COMETFIT_DATA_KEY: ${COMETFIT_DATA_KEY:-Q29tZXRGaXQtZGV2LW9ubHkta2V5LWNoYW5nZS1tZSE=}
      COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY: ${COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY:-dev-integration-key}
      COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO: ${COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO:-true}
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD-SHELL", "wget -qO- http://localhost:8080/actuator/health || exit 1"]
      interval: 5s
      timeout: 3s
      retries: 30

A-35 | (stage 2) Water inputs that LogWater does not cover: missing amount, an amount that truncates to 0.00 L, very large amounts, ml input, floating-point truncation error | Missing -> 400 "Amount is required." EOF

26. EOF

# Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. # Assumptions

Every gap that had to be filled because `spec/` (Project Proposal = "Prop", Deliverable 1 = "D1", Deliverable 2 draft = "D2",
team repo code = "TRC", team decisions = "TD-n") is silent or ambiguous. Code comments reference these IDs.
Rows answered by a later input are kept and marked **SUPERSEDED by ...** (stage 2).

A-n | what was missing | choice made | related spec section
---|---|---|---
A-1 | How the "Server" box (API gateway, auth gateway, 4 services, encrypted DB) is deployed; load balancing / telemetry details | One Spring Boot process with one package per box: `gateway` (API gateway + module routing), `security` (auth gateway), `controllers`+`services` (Social / Activity / Nutrition / Admin), PostgreSQL. Load balancing is not built for a laptop demo; telemetry = health checks + uptime records (FR-1). | D1 §5.3.1, §5.3.2, §5.3.3
A-2 | Which database product; Docker Engine not running on the build machine | PostgreSQL 16 (docker-compose) is the default. An `h2` Spring profile (embedded file DB, PostgreSQL mode) lets the app run and be tested without Docker. The same Flyway schema is used for both. | D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"; Prop §9 "Database for the app" **SUPERSEDED by `spec/04-team-repo-code/README.md` ("MySQL for database operations") and `db/docker-compose.yml` (`mysql:8.4`): database is now MySQL 8.4; see A-33.**
A-3 | How accounts are created (every use case includes "Log In" but there is no sign-up use case) | Students self-register (username, password, email, display name) and get a TOTP secret to add to an authenticator app. Developer accounts are created by seed/config only. | D1 Fig 4.3 "Log In (Password + TOTP)"; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (TOTP setup part) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (1), (2): after sign-up the app shows "Add to authenticator app" and "Copy setup key", and a QR code only on larger screens; self-registration itself is unchanged. See A-39.**
A-4 | Credential rules | Username 3–30 chars `[A-Za-z0-9_.]`, unique (case-insensitive); password ≥ 8 chars; email must look like an address. | NFR Security
A-5 | What "all user data will be encrypted" means concretely | Passwords: BCrypt hash. Email and TOTP secret: AES-256-GCM field encryption (key from `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`). Other tables (meals, steps, …) rely on database/disk-level encryption in a real deployment, because the app must sum and query them. TLS is expected from the deployment's reverse proxy; the local demo uses plain HTTP. | NFR Security, NFR Legislative-Security; D1 §5.3.2 "Encrypted Database"
A-6 | Login flow detail and session lifetime | One login call carries username + password + 6-digit TOTP code; a Session (random 256-bit token, Bearer header) is created only if both factors pass, and lasts 12 h. `AuthService.authenticate` therefore takes the TOTP code as a third argument. TOTP = RFC 6238, SHA-1, 30 s, ±1 step. | D1 §5.2 AuthService, Session; NFR Security **SUPERSEDED (code on every sign-in) by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-1.md` (3): "Remember this device for 30 days"; a remembered device signs in with username + password only. Session lifetime and TOTP parameters unchanged. See A-39.**
A-7 | Default goals for a new student | 2000 kcal, 2000 ml water, 10 000 steps, 500 ml bottle. Students can change them. | D1 §5.2 Student (calorieGoal, waterGoalMl, stepGoal)
A-8 | Where the water-bottle size lives (Prop: "volume of the user's water bottle … number of refills"; SD-1 "log water (bottle size / refill)"; class diagram has no field) | Added `bottleSizeMl` to Student (set in Profile → Goals). The app logs a refill as `saveWaterEntry(bottleSizeMl)`, plus half bottle or a custom amount. | Prop §4; D1 SD-1
A-9 | What "daily" means (time zone of the day boundary) | Configurable `COMETFIT_ZONE`, default America/Chicago (D1 cites the Texas Data Privacy and Security Act, so the users are in Texas). | D1 UC-1 "View Daily Summary & Goals"
A-10 | Thresholds for an "unsafe goal" | Warn when calorie goal < 1200 or > 4000 kcal, water goal < 1000 or > 4000 ml, step goal > 30 000 (Prop risk "User over-exertion → Warnings of the app"). The goal is still saved; the app only warns (NFR says "allow a warning"). | D1 NFR Safety; Prop §8
A-11 | Which "portions of the app" can be shut down | Three modules, each mapped to an API prefix: NUTRITION (`/api/nutrition`), ACTIVITY (`/api/activity`), SOCIAL (`/api/social`). Login, profile and admin cannot be disabled. A disabled module answers 503 `MODULE_DISABLED`, and the client shows a maintenance notice on those tabs. | FR-5; D1 UC-4, SD-4 ("disable module (e.g. Friends)")
A-12 | How external systems (UREC card reader, monitoring service) authenticate | Shared secret in header `X-Integration-Key` (`COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`). Card readers must also be registered in `urec_card_readers`; seed reader `UREC-FRONT-1` at "UREC front desk". | D1 §5.3.2 External Systems; SD-2, SD-4; NFR Security
A-13 | Names and contents of the "backend permissions list" | Students implicitly hold `nutrition.use`, `activity.use`, `social.use`, `profile.use`. Developers hold an explicit list; the seeded developer has `admin.uptime.view`, `admin.modules.manage`, `profile.use`. Developers do not get student features. | D1 NFR Security; §5.2 Developer.permissions; UC-4 "Authorize Admin (Permissions + TOTP)"
A-14 | Data for a recorded demo | When `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO=true` (default), seed developer `dev` and students `alice` and `bob`, password `CometFit123!`, with fixed, published TOTP secrets. Demo only; turn it off anywhere real. | PROMPT (demoable in a video)
A-15 | Behaviour of the "AI Food Recognition Service" | Stub: picks 1–2 entries from a fixed placeholder table, deterministically from the image's SHA-256. The estimate is shown for review and is saved only after the student confirms or edits it. The photo itself is not stored. | D1 UC-1 "Log Meal by Photo"; SD-1; Prop §2
A-16 | UTD Dining menu content and locations | Stub feed with two locations, "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" (from FR-8's rationale "campus stores and dining hall"), and 5 placeholder items each. Each `getMenu` call refreshes items from the feed into `dining_items` (keyed by the feed's item id), so meal entries can reference them. | FR-8; D1 UC-1 "Maintain Dining Menu & Macros"; §5.2 DiningItem
A-17 | Meaning of `steps` in a pushed ActivityRecord | Steps counted since the previous sync (an increment). Daily steps = sum of the day's records. Limits per push: steps 0–100 000, heart rate 20–250 bpm. | D1 SD-2 "pushSteps(steps, heartRate, timestamp)"; §5.2 ActivityRecord
A-18 | Default data-sharing consent | All four `share*` flags default to false; nothing is visible to friends until the student turns it on. | D1 NFR Legislative-Privacy; §5.2 ConsentSettings **SUPERSEDED for the seeded demo accounts only by `spec/03-team-decisions/TD-2.md`: alice and bob start with all four sharing flags on. Real new accounts keep everything off (this row still applies to them). See A-40.**
A-19 | When water intake is "too low" (FR-6 verification) | Any time today's total is below the student's water goal, the daily summary includes a "water intake is low" message. Reaching the goal shows a "goal reached" message instead. | FR-6 RTM verification method (D1 §4.4)
A-20 | Point values and limits | UREC visit: 10 points, awarded only for the first visit of each day (later swipes are still recorded). Reaching the daily step goal: 5 points, once per day. Points are never deducted. | Prop §3 "point based system"; D1 UC-2 "Earn Points", SD-2 `awardPoints(studentId, VISIT)`
A-21 | What the leaderboard ranks and who appears on it | Rank = point balance (ties share a rank), among the student and their friends. Points come only from visits and steps, so a friend appears (and their points show in their stats) only if they share visits or steps. | D1 UC-3 "View Leaderboard"; NFR Legislative-Privacy; Prop §7 leaderboard
A-22 | What `isPublic` controls | Non-friends viewing a private profile see only the username, not the display name or member-since date. Search by username always works, so friend requests are still possible. | D1 §5.2 User.isPublic; FR-3; Prop §4 "user-entered public information"
A-23 | How the friend is "notified of request" (Prop excludes push notifications) | In-app only: the request appears in the receiver's *Friend requests* list. | D1 SD-3 "notify of request"; Prop §4 Out of Scope
A-24 | Delivery channel for downtime alerts and when to send one | Stub `LoggingAlertNotifier`: logs a WARN line and keeps the last 50 alerts for the admin dashboard. An alert fires when a service goes down (first down check) and again when it recovers, not on every check. | D1 UC-4 "Raise Downtime Alert"; SD-4 alt [service down]
A-25 | Which "servers" are monitored, how often, how long records are kept | 7 components named after the §5.3.2 boxes (api-gateway, auth-gateway, nutrition-service, activity-service, social-service, admin-service, database), each with a real probe. Checks run every 30 s (configurable); uptime % is the share of successful checks over the chosen window (default 24 h). Records are kept 30 days. | FR-1; D1 SD-4 loop [every interval]; §5.2 MonitoringService.checkIntervalSec
A-26 | Client technology, given "mobile app only, no web application" (Prop §4, §7) vs. the requirement that the demo runs in a browser | Cross-platform Expo / React Native app (NFR Development: "native or cross-platform mobile app"). The same app is run through react-native-web for the laptop demo; this is a way to run the mobile client, not a separate web product. The phone-sized layout is kept. | Prop §4 Out of Scope; D1 NFR Operational, NFR Development; PROMPT
A-27 | What the UREC card carries to identify the student | The card reader sends the student's CometFit user id as `studentId` (the class diagram has no separate card-number field). | D1 SD-2 `recordVisit(studentId, time)`; §5.2 UrecCardReader.sendSwipe(studentId)
A-28 | Smart-device link rules | A health-data permission must be granted before linking (UC-2 «include» Grant Health Permissions). A device can be LINKED to only one student at a time. Optional automatic sync runs every 60 s while the Activity screen is open. | D1 UC-2, SD-2; NFR Interoperability

A-30 | Range of friend statistics | A friend's stats show today's calories, water and steps (with goals), UREC visits in the last 7 days, point balance, and leaderboard rank, each only if consented. | D1 UC-3 "View Friend's Statistics"; SD-3

## 4. Run the project locally

### Start the database and server

**Option A — PostgreSQL in Docker (default profile)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up -d db          # PostgreSQL 16 on localhost:5432
cd server
mvn spring-boot:run
```

**Option B — no Docker (embedded H2 file database)**

```bash
cd app/server
mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=h2
```

Either way, Flyway creates the schema on first start. The server is ready when
<http://localhost:8080/actuator/health> shows `{"status":"UP"}`. The H2 data is stored in `app/server/data/`;
delete that folder to start over.

*(Optional: run everything in containers with `docker compose --profile full up -d --build`.)*

### Start the client

```bash
cd app/client
npm run web            # opens http://localhost:8081 in the browser
```

For a phone-like view in the browser, use the dev tools' device toolbar. On a real phone, run `npx expo start` and
open the app in Expo Go. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to your laptop's LAN address, for example
`http://192.168.1.20:8080`.

### Sign in

| Username | Password | TOTP secret | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alice` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITALICE234` | Student |
| `bob` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITBOBBY567` | Student |
| `dev` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITDEVADMIN` | Developer (admin dashboard) |

Every sign-in needs the current 6-digit code. Get it from any authenticator app (add the secret), or from:

```bash
node app/tools/totp.mjs COMETFITALICE234
```

New students can register from the sign-in screen. The app then shows their own TOTP secret once.

## 5. Run the tests

```bash
cd app/server && mvn test        # 38 API/unit tests on H2, one test class per use case (Uc1..Uc4) + security
cd app/client && npm test        # client unit tests (Node test runner)
cd app/client && npm run typecheck

# End-to-end over real HTTP against a running server (uses the demo accounts):
node app/tools/smoke.mjs http://localhost:8080
```

## 6. Demo script (about 5 minutes)

1. **UC-1** — Sign in as `alice`. On **Log**, tap *+1 refill*, then log a meal manually. Switch to *Dining menu* →
   *Dining Hall* → *Add* an item. Switch to *Photo (AI)* and pick any image, edit the estimate, then *Confirm & save*.
   **Today** shows calories, macros, water progress and the low-water message.
2. **Safety** — in **Profile → Daily goals**, enter 800 kcal or 6000 ml and watch the warnings appear.
3. **UC-2** — **Activity** → *Connect smart device* → *Allow* (simulated health prompt) → *Sync now*. Then
   *Simulate UREC card swipe*, which earns +10 points and appears in the visit history.
4. **UC-3** — **Friends** → search `bob` → *Profile* → *Add friend*. In a second browser window (or a private
   window), sign in as `bob` and *Accept*. As `alice`, turn sharing on under *What my friends can see*. As `bob`,
   open alice's *Stats* and the leaderboard.
5. **UC-4** — Sign in as `dev`. The dashboard shows uptime % and per-service status. Click *Simulate outage* on a
   service to see a downtime alert and an incident, then end it. *Disable* "Friends & Leaderboard" and switch to
   bob's window: the Friends tab shows the maintenance notice while the other tabs keep working. *Re-enable* it.

## 7. Stubs (external systems from the spec)

| External actor in the spec | Interface | Stub implementation |
|---|---|---|
| AI Food Recognition Service (UC-1) | `services/AIFoodService` | `stubs/FakeAIFoodService` — deterministic estimate from the image hash |
| UTD Dining menu data (UC-1, FR-8) | `services/UtdDiningFeed` | `stubs/StubUtdDiningFeed` — fixed sample menu for "Dining Hall" and "Campus Store" |
| Smart Device pairing (UC-2) | `services/SmartDeviceGateway` | `stubs/FakeSmartDeviceGateway` — always pairs, except device ids starting with `FAIL` |
| Smart Device readings + health permission (UC-2) | client `src/smartDevice.ts` `SmartDeviceAdapter` | `FakeSmartDevice` — simulated steps / heart rate |
| UREC Card Reader (UC-2) | `POST /api/activity/visits` with the integration key | `stubs/FakeUrecCardReader` — the "Simulate UREC card swipe" button |
| Monitoring Service (UC-4) | `POST /api/admin/health-check` with the integration key | `stubs/MonitoringAgentStub` — timer inside the server |

# CometFit — local setup and demo guide

CometFit (SE 3354 Team 9) is a student health-tracking app: meals and water (UC-1), activity and UREC visits (UC-2),
friends' progress (UC-3), and developer monitoring and control (UC-4). It was built only from the team's Proposal,
Deliverable 1, the Deliverable 2 draft, the team's water-logging unit code, and team decisions TD-1..TD-3 (all in `../spec/`). `../TRACEABILITY.md` maps every requirement to code and tests. `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` lists every gap
that had to be filled.

```
app/
├── server/            Spring Boot REST server: API gateway, auth gateway, Nutrition / Activity / Social / Admin services
├── client/            Expo (React Native) mobile app — also runs in a web browser for the demo
├── tools/             totp.mjs (prints sign-in codes), smoke.mjs (end-to-end HTTP check)
└── docker-compose.yml MySQL 8.4 database + the server
```

The architecture follows Deliverable 1 §5.3 (client-server): the mobile client talks to one REST API, and every call
goes through the auth gateway (password + TOTP sessions, permissions list) and the module (feature-flag) check before
it reaches a service. Outside systems (AI food recognition, UTD Dining menus, smart devices, the UREC card reader,
the monitoring service and the alert channel) are **stubs**. They are labelled `*** STUB ***` in the code and listed at
the end of this file.

---

## 1. Install prerequisites

| Tool | Version used | Check with |
|---|---|---|
| Java JDK | 21 or newer (built with 23) | `java -version` |
| Maven | 3.9+ | `mvn -v` |
| Node.js + npm | Node 22+ | `node -v` |
| Docker Desktop | recommended (MySQL + server) | `docker version` |

Without Docker, use the embedded H2 database (step 4, option B).

## 2. Install dependencies

```bash
# server (downloads the Maven dependencies)
cd app/server
mvn -DskipTests package

# client
cd ../client
npm install
```

## 3. Configure environment variables

Every variable has a development default, so **nothing needs to be set for a local demo**. For anything shared, set
at least `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` and `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`.

### Server (`app/server`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/cometfit` (H2 file `./data/cometfit-mysql` with the `h2` profile) | JDBC URL |
| `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` | `cometfit` / `cometfit` | Database login |
| `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` | `root` | MySQL root password (docker-compose only) |
| `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` | development key | Base64 32-byte AES key that encrypts emails and TOTP secrets at rest. Generate one: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`. **Changing it makes existing accounts unreadable.** |
| `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY` | `dev-integration-key` | Shared secret that the UREC card reader and the external monitor send in the `X-Integration-Key` header |
| `COMETFIT_ZONE` | `America/Chicago` | Time zone that defines "today" for daily totals |
| `COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS` | `12` | Session lifetime |
| `COMETFIT_REMEMBER_DEVICE_DAYS` | `30` | How long "Remember this device" skips the 6-digit code (TD-1) |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC` | `30` | Health-check interval of the monitoring stub |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB` | `true` | Run the built-in monitoring-service stub |
| `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO` | `true` | Create the demo accounts below on start-up |
| `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006` | Browser origins allowed to call the API |

### Client (`app/client`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` (`http://10.0.2.2:8080` on the Android emulator) | Server base URL |

To set variables: in bash, `export NAME=value`. In PowerShell, `$env:NAME = "value"`. You can also put client
variables in `app/client/.env` (this file is git-ignored).

## 4. Run the project locally

### Start the database and server

**Option A — PostgreSQL in Docker (default profile)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up -d db          # PostgreSQL 16 on localhost:5432
cd server
mvn spring-boot:run
```

**Option B — no Docker (embedded H2 file database)**

```bash
cd app/server
mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=h2
```

Either way, Flyway creates the schema on first start. The server is ready when
<http://localhost:8080/actuator/health> shows `{"status":"UP"}`. The H2 data is stored in `app/server/data/`;
delete that folder to start over.

```bash
cd app/client
npm run web            # opens http://localhost:8081 in the browser
```

For a phone-like view in the browser, use the dev tools' device toolbar. On a real phone, run `npx expo start` and
open the app in Expo Go. Set `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` to your laptop's LAN address, for example
`http://192.168.1.20:8080`.

| Username | Password | TOTP secret | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| `alice` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITALICE234` | Student |
| `bob` | `CometFit123!` | `COMETFITBOBBY567` | Student |

## 5. Run the tests

```bash

## 6. Demo script (about 5 minutes)

1. **UC-1** — Sign in as `alice`. On **Log**, tap *+1 refill*, then log a meal manually. Switch to *Dining menu* →
   *Dining Hall* → *Add* an item. Switch to *Photo (AI)* and pick any image, edit the estimate, then *Confirm & save*.
   **Today** shows calories, macros, water progress and the low-water message.
2. **Safety** — in **Profile → Daily goals**, enter 800 kcal or 6000 ml and watch the warnings appear.
3. **UC-2** — **Activity** → *Connect smart device* → *Allow* (simulated health prompt) → *Sync now*. Then
   *Simulate UREC card swipe*, which earns +10 points and appears in the visit history.

   service to see a downtime alert and an incident, then end it. *Disable* "Friends & Leaderboard" and switch to

# CometFit — local setup and demo guide

CometFit (SE 3354 Team 9) is a student health-tracking app: meals and water (UC-1), activity and UREC visits (UC-2),
friends' progress (UC-3), and developer monitoring and control (UC-4). It was built only from the team's Proposal,
Deliverable 1, the Deliverable 2 draft, the team's water-logging unit code, and team decisions TD-1..TD-3 (all in `../spec/`). `../TRACEABILITY.md` maps every requirement to code and tests. `../ASSUMPTIONS.md` lists every gap
that had to be filled.

```
app/
├── server/            Spring Boot REST server: API gateway, auth gateway, Nutrition / Activity / Social / Admin services
├── client/            Expo (React Native) mobile app — also runs in a web browser for the demo
├── tools/             totp.mjs (prints sign-in codes), smoke.mjs (end-to-end HTTP check)
└── docker-compose.yml MySQL 8.4 database + the server
```

The architecture follows Deliverable 1 §5.3 (client-server): the mobile client talks to one REST API, and every call
goes through the auth gateway (password + TOTP sessions, permissions list) and the module (feature-flag) check before
it reaches a service. Outside systems (AI food recognition, UTD Dining menus, smart devices, the UREC card reader,
the monitoring service and the alert channel) are **stubs**. They are labelled `*** STUB ***` in the code and listed at
the end of this file.

---

## 1. Install prerequisites

| Tool | Version used | Check with |
|---|---|---|
| Java JDK | 21 or newer (built with 23) | `java -version` |
| Maven | 3.9+ | `mvn -v` |
| Node.js + npm | Node 22+ | `node -v` |
| Docker Desktop | recommended (MySQL + server) | `docker version` |

Without Docker, use the embedded H2 database (step 4, option B).

## 2. Install dependencies

```bash
# server (downloads the Maven dependencies)
cd app/server
mvn -DskipTests package

# client
cd ../client
npm install
```

## 3. Configure environment variables

Every variable has a development default, so **nothing needs to be set for a local demo**. For anything shared, set
at least `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` and `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY`.

### Server (`app/server`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `PORT` | `8080` | HTTP port |
| `DB_URL` | `jdbc:mysql://localhost:3306/cometfit` (H2 file `./data/cometfit-mysql` with the `h2` profile) | JDBC URL |
| `DB_USER` / `DB_PASSWORD` | `cometfit` / `cometfit` | Database login |
| `DB_ROOT_PASSWORD` | `root` | MySQL root password (docker-compose only) |
| `COMETFIT_DATA_KEY` | development key | Base64 32-byte AES key that encrypts emails and TOTP secrets at rest. Generate one: `node -e "console.log(require('crypto').randomBytes(32).toString('base64'))"`. **Changing it makes existing accounts unreadable.** |
| `COMETFIT_INTEGRATION_KEY` | `dev-integration-key` | Shared secret that the UREC card reader and the external monitor send in the `X-Integration-Key` header |
| `COMETFIT_ZONE` | `America/Chicago` | Time zone that defines "today" for daily totals |
| `COMETFIT_SESSION_HOURS` | `12` | Session lifetime |
| `COMETFIT_REMEMBER_DEVICE_DAYS` | `30` | How long "Remember this device" skips the 6-digit code (TD-1) |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_INTERVAL_SEC` | `30` | Health-check interval of the monitoring stub |
| `COMETFIT_MONITOR_STUB` | `true` | Run the built-in monitoring-service stub |
| `COMETFIT_SEED_DEMO` | `true` | Create the demo accounts below on start-up |
| `COMETFIT_CORS_ORIGINS` | `http://localhost:8081,http://localhost:19006` | Browser origins allowed to call the API |

### Client (`app/client`)

| Variable | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` | `http://localhost:8080` (`http://10.0.2.2:8080` on the Android emulator) | Server base URL |

To set variables: in bash, `export NAME=value`. In PowerShell, `$env:NAME = "value"`. You can also put client
variables in `app/client/.env` (this file is git-ignored).

## 4. Run the project locally

### Start the database and server

**Option A — everything in Docker (recommended)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up --build        # MySQL 8.4 on localhost:3306 + the server on localhost:8080
```

Add `-d` to run it in the background. The server waits until MySQL is healthy. The first build downloads the Maven
dependencies inside the image, so it takes a few minutes.

**Option A2 — MySQL in Docker, server from Maven (for development)**

```bash
cd app
docker compose up -d db
cd server
mvn spring-boot:run
```

**Option B — no Docker (embedded H2 file database in MySQL mode)**

```bash

mvn spring-boot:run -Dspring-boot.run.profiles=h2
```

Flyway creates the schema on first start (`V1` schema, `V2` water log in liters, `V3` remembered devices). The server
is ready when <http://localhost:8080/actuator/health> shows `{"status":"UP"}`.

**Start the demo over with clean data** (removes everything, including test leftovers, then re-seeds the demo accounts):

```bash

docker compose down -v           # -v deletes the MySQL volume
